body:
Confirmed by the §58 S1 audit (loam-scan-scale, verified, three sites): a bound connection's read resolves through `connectionScope`, which walks this store's whole ground to decide membership and composes EVERY sibling inbox pool in full. There is no warm path — the materialization is maintained over the primary and cannot answer a container's question, so `gatherImpl` takes the cold branch for every bound request. A bound listing pays that walk once per page AND again per listed entity; a REST clear pays it once per named field. The cost is stated honestly in `listing.ts` today; this ticket is the fix.

This is the shape T163 built the maintained candidate set to escape, and a container has none. Build the same instrument for a container scope, with the same two-sided rail T163 earned:

- FAST = SLOW: every page the maintained set serves is the page a cold `connectionScope` projection serves, on this gateway AND on a fresh gateway opened over the same backend.
- EVERY PATH THAT CHANGES MEMBERSHIP REACHES THE INDEX (H8's stale-index trap): a plain append, an inbox-pool write, a strike, a revived strike, a strike arriving before its target, an exclusion and its re-inclusion, a pool attached or dropped, an erasure that reseats the reactor.
- The cost assertion is deterministic and spied, never timed.

Verify: test/gateway/binding-scale.test.ts (new), and the existing test/gateway/listing-warm.test.ts shape as the model. Belongs with S2's container tools, where containers gain their own lifecycle.
title: A maintained candidate set for a bound container's reads
